engine_name: Scene Environmental Continuity & World-State Memory Director
purpose: Persist validated environmental and world-state consequences across scenes, reconstruct location state on re-entry, track recovery and repair, and prevent silent environmental resets.
core_principle: A location remembers validated consequences; returning to a place restores its latest canonical environmental state unless an explicit intervening event changes it.
memory_model: validated_world_delta + location_identity + narrative_time + causal_history → persistent_world_memory → scene_reentry_snapshot

location_memory_schema.rule: Location memory is authoritative for persistent environmental state and is updated only by validated world-state transitions.

world_state_schema.version_rule: Every accepted environmental change creates a new location-state version; prior versions remain auditable.

memory_entry_schema.rule: Only VALIDATED deltas enter persistent world memory.

reentry_reconstruction.rule: Re-entry state is reconstructed from the latest canonical location state plus all validated intervening events and recovery transitions.

recovery_and_repair.rule: Recovery cannot erase history; it creates a new validated transition while preserving the prior consequence.

cross_scene_continuity.rule: Every scene entering an existing location must reconcile requested scene state against persistent world memory before production.

historical_integrity.rule: World history is append-only; no silent overwrite or deletion of prior environmental consequences.

world_memory_hierarchy.location: Authoritative for local geography and environmental state.
world_memory_hierarchy.region: Aggregates validated consequences affecting multiple locations or regional conditions.
world_memory_hierarchy.world: Stores validated global conditions such as war state, climate-scale events or civilization-level changes.
world_memory_hierarchy.precedence: More local state overrides broader state only where the local domain is explicitly defined; otherwise broader state propagates.

continuity_rules: Transient effects may resolve without entering long-term active state.
Resolved effects remain in history even after disappearance.
A location re-entry cannot use the original baseline if persistent changes exist.
Narrative time determines which recovery events have occurred.
Future environmental events cannot affect earlier scene snapshots.
Scene-specific temporary VFX do not become permanent world memory unless CSD-025 marks them persistent.
World memory cannot mutate character identity, anatomy or costume.
Variant timelines require explicit variant/revision identifiers.
Every reconstructed state must be traceable to validated source deltas.
Maximum five active characters remains enforced.
